title: MANICOUAGAN EYE

beats.text: This bright blue ring, seventy kilometers across, hides a massive crater beneath.
From orbit the lake looks like a bright blue eye amid dark forest.
The water forms a seventy-kilometer circle, while the crater spans about one hundred kilometers.
So why does this ancient scar appear as such a perfect circle?
A meteor five kilometers across hit here two hundred fourteen million years ago.
The impact made a multi-ring basin; rain and rivers later filled the centre, creating the lake.
It now holds about one hundred thirty-eight cubic kilometers of water, enough to flood a city.
That smooth ring you see is the scar of a cosmic collision.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: Manicouagan Reservoir is a seventy‑kilometer‑wide annular lake formed by a five‑kilometer meteor impact 214 million years ago. It fills a multi‑ring crater about one hundred kilometers across and holds roughly 138 cubic kilometers of water. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: NASA, Wikimedia Commons.
